item.title: Iran war wipes $11.5 trillion from global markets in one month
item.description: One month after the United States and Israel launched a joint military campaign against Iran on February 28, the conflict has wiped $11.5 trillion from global stock markets and sent energy prices surging, reshaping the economic outlook for much of the world.

item.title: Hormuz oil crisis intensifies global push for renewables
item.description: Nearly a month after Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to commercial shipping, the worst global energy disruption in decades is intensifying calls from governments, international agencies, and industry groups to accelerate the transition to renewable energy.

item.title: Japan backs US deep sea mining push in new pact
item.description:
The United States and Japan have signed a memorandum of cooperation on deep sea mining, agreeing to share research and support each other's ventures into the emerging industry. The non-legally binding agreement, signed following a meeting between President Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Washington on March 19, was subsequently circulated at a semiannual session of the International Seabed Authority, where 170 nations have spent a decade trying to agree on rules for mining the ocean floor.

The partnership represents the first major international endorsement of recent U.S. efforts to pursue seabed mining, which Washington has advanced largely on its own since early 2025. Diplomats and officials working on seabed issues described the agreement as an extraordinary public show of support for the American push.

item.title: MIT, ASU teams crack protein motion design for drug discovery
item.description: Two research teams have independently developed methods to design and study proteins based on how they move rather than how they look, a shift that could reshape drug discovery by treating molecular dynamics as a core design parameter.

item.title: NASA days from launching first crewed moon mission since 1972
item.description: NASA is entering one of its busiest stretches in decades, with a nuclear-powered Mars spacecraft set for a December 2028 launch and the first crewed mission to the moon in more than 50 years just days away.

item.title: NeurIPS reverses ban on Chinese researchers after boycott threat
item.description:
The Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, the world's premier machine learning conference, reversed a controversial policy barring submissions from U.S.-sanctioned entities on Friday after China's leading academic and science organizations announced boycotts and called on domestic researchers to disengage entirely from the event.

NeurIPS said in a statement posted to X and its official website that the broad restrictions had been "published by mistake because of a miscommunication" with its legal team, and that the policy now applies only to individuals on the U.S. Treasury's Specially Designated Nationals list — a narrower scope than originally indicated. "The responsibility for that error is ours as an organization, and we deeply apologize for the alarm and impact this miscommunication had on our community," the conference said.

item.title: Drones strike Oman's Salalah port again, injuring worker
item.description: Two unmanned aerial vehicles struck the Port of Salalah in southern Oman on Saturday, injuring an expatriate worker and causing limited damage to a crane, according to the Oman News Agency. Omani officials condemned the attack and pledged to take all necessary measures to protect the country's security and the safety of its residents.

item.title: Drones hit Kuwait airport again, heavily damaging radar system
item.description:
Kuwait International Airport was struck by multiple drones early Saturday, causing major damage to its radar system in the latest attack on the Gulf state's primary aviation hub, according to the country's civil aviation authority.

Abdullah Al-Rajhi, spokesperson for Kuwait's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), told the Kuwait News Agency (KUNA) that the airport "was subjected to several drone attacks, but no casualties were reported". He said the strikes resulted in "major damage to the airport's radar system" and that emergency response teams were immediately deployed to assess the situation and work toward restoring operational readiness.

item.title: IDF says it killed two senior Hezbollah operatives in Lebanon strikes
item.description: The Israel Defense Forces announced Saturday that it killed two senior members of Hezbollah's communications unit in strikes carried out the previous day, as cross-border hostilities between Israel and the Lebanese militant group showed no signs of abating nearly four weeks into the broader regional conflict.

item.title: Iran demands UN accountability over strikes on oil infrastructure
item.description: Iran's ambassador to the United Nations has launched a diplomatic offensive at the world body, filing formal complaints over US-Israeli military strikes on Iranian energy facilities and warning of alleged assassination plots targeting senior government officials, as the conflict that began on February 28 enters its second month.

item.title: Poland extends border checks with Germany, Lithuania until October
item.description: Poland announced on Saturday that it will extend temporary border controls along its frontiers with Germany and Lithuania by six months, keeping the checks in place until October 1. The decision prolongs what has become an increasingly entrenched suspension of the Schengen Area's open-border regime, with Warsaw citing persistent irregular migration and internal security concerns as justification.

item.title: French police foil bomb attack outside Bank of America in Paris
item.description: French police thwarted an attempted bombing outside Bank of America offices in Paris early Saturday morning, arresting one suspect as he prepared to ignite a homemade explosive device, according to sources close to the investigation cited by Agence France-Presse. A second suspect fled the scene and remains at large.

item.title: Israeli forces push 8 km into south Lebanon toward Litani River
item.description: Israeli ground forces have advanced roughly eight kilometers into southern Lebanon along the coast toward the town of Bayada, according to a United Nations official and Lebanon's defense minister, as Israel's military leadership signals its intent to seize and hold territory stretching to the Litani River — an area amounting to nearly a tenth of the country.

item.title: Zelenskyy signs 10-year defense pact with Qatar, capping Gulf tour
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrapped up a whirlwind three-day tour of the Gulf this week, signing defense cooperation agreements with Saudi Arabia and Qatar and reaching a security pact with the United Arab Emirates — all while pressing oil-rich partners to help avert a looming diesel crisis back home.

item.title: Iranian strike damages major UAE aluminum plant, workers injured
item.description: Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah site in Abu Dhabi, the largest aluminum-producing complex in the United Arab Emirates, sustained significant damage on Saturday during Iranian missile and drone attacks, according to a Reuters report. A number of workers at the facility were injured in the strike, Aluminium Today reported.

item.title: IDF needs 'a few more weeks' to degrade Iran's military, Israeli official says
item.description: A senior Israeli security official told ABC News that the Israel Defense Forces need "a few more weeks" to fully degrade Iranian military capabilities, casting doubt on the prospect of a swift diplomatic resolution to the month-old war even as President Donald Trump extended a deadline threatening Iran's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Explosion hits near Erbil airport as Kurdistan attacks persist
item.description: An explosion was heard Saturday morning near the international airport of Erbil, the capital of Iraq's autonomous Kurdistan Region, according to an AFP journalist on the ground. A witness reported seeing smoke rising from the area near the airport perimeter. No details on casualties or the cause of the blast were immediately available.

item.title: Trump weighs stripping NATO voting rights over Iran war dispute
item.description: President Donald Trump escalated his confrontation with NATO on Friday, telling a major investment conference in Miami that the United States may no longer come to the defense of alliance members who refused to support American military operations against Iran. Speaking at the Future Investment Initiative Priority Summit on March 27, Trump called NATO allies' absence from the now month-old conflict a "tremendous mistake" and questioned the fundamental bargain underpinning the 77-year-old alliance.

item.title: Houthis fire missiles at Israel, warn of Red Sea blockade
item.description:
Yemen's Houthi rebels launched their first missile attack on Israel early Saturday, firing a barrage of ballistic missiles at what they described as "sensitive Israeli military installations" in the country's south, and warned that closing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait remains on the table — a move that could compound what is already a severe global energy crisis.

The Israeli military said it intercepted a missile launched from Yemen, reporting no casualties. Brigadier General Yahya Saree, the Houthi military spokesperson, claimed responsibility in a broadcast on the group's Al-Masirah channel, declaring the attacks would continue "until the aggression on all resistance fronts comes to a halt". The strikes mark the Houthis' formal entry into the month-old war between the United States, Israel, and Iran.

item.title: Israeli airstrike kills three journalists in southern Lebanon
item.description:
An Israeli airstrike on a media vehicle near the town of Jezzine in southern Lebanon killed at least three journalists on Saturday, according to Lebanese media reports, in one of the deadliest single attacks on press workers since the current round of fighting began in early March.

Ali Shoeib, a prominent correspondent for the Hezbollah-affiliated Al-Manar TV, and Fatima Ftouni, a reporter for Al-Mayadeen, were among those killed when the strike hit the car they were traveling in. A third victim, reported to be Ftouni's brother and cameraman, also died in the attack, according to the Lebanese newspaper L'Orient-Le Jour, as cited by Spain's El País. A fourth occupant, identified as Shoeib's son, was also in the vehicle.
